title: MATH GAOKAO - 341
description: Authentic-style mathematics problems inspired by China’s Gaokao — build deeper understanding, sharper thinking, and real exam readiness.

questions.concept: Interquartile Range from a Box Plot
questions.learningObjective: Compute the interquartile range from the five-number summary of a box plot.
questions.question: A box plot has five-number summary \(2,5,7,9,12\). Find the interquartile range.
questions.explanation: The interquartile range is \(Q_3-Q_1\). Here \(Q_1=5\) and \(Q_3=9\), so \(\mathrm{IQR}=9-5=4\).
questions.hint: Recall that the box in a box plot extends from \(Q_1\) to \(Q_3\), so its length is the interquartile range.

questions.learningObjective: Compute the range of a data set from the five-number summary shown in a box plot.
questions.question: A box plot has five-number summary \(3,6,10,14,20\). Find the range of the data.
questions.explanation: The range is the difference between the maximum and minimum values. Here the minimum is \(3\) and the maximum is \(20\), so the range is \(20-3=17\).
questions.hint: The whiskers extend to the minimum and maximum values when there are no outliers, so use those two values.

questions.concept: Upper Whisker Length in a Box Plot
questions.learningObjective: Compute the length of the upper whisker from the upper quartile and maximum value.
questions.question: In a box plot with \(Q_3=15\) and maximum \(=23\), assuming the maximum is not an outlier, what is the length of the upper whisker?
questions.explanation: The upper whisker extends from \(Q_3\) to the maximum value when the maximum is not an outlier. Its length is \(23-15=8\).
questions.hint: The upper whisker connects the right edge of the box, \(Q_3\), to the largest non-outlier value.

questions.concept: Middle 50 Percent in a Box Plot
questions.learningObjective: Identify the interval containing the middle 50 percent of the data from a box plot.
questions.question: A box plot has five-number summary \(4,8,12,16,20\). Which interval contains the middle \(50\%\) of the data?
questions.explanation: In a box plot, the box contains the middle \(50\%\) of the data. The box extends from the lower quartile \(Q_1=8\) to the upper quartile \(Q_3=16\), so the interval is \([8,16]\).
questions.hint: The middle \(50\%\) of the data lies between the first and third quartiles.

questions.concept: Comparing Box Plots by Interquartile Range
questions.learningObjective: Compare two box plots by computing and comparing their interquartile ranges.
questions.question: Class A has five-number summary \(50,60,70,80,90\). Class B has five-number summary \(50,55,75,85,90\). Which class has the larger interquartile range?
questions.explanation: For Class A, \(\mathrm{IQR}=80-60=20\). For Class B, \(\mathrm{IQR}=85-55=30\). Since \(30>20\), Class B has the larger interquartile range.
questions.hint: Compute \(Q_3-Q_1\) for each class and compare the two results.

questions.learningObjective: Use the \(1.5\times \mathrm{IQR}\) rule to determine whether a value is an outlier.
questions.question: A box plot has \(Q_1=20\) and \(Q_3=50\). Using the \(1.5\times \mathrm{IQR}\) rule, which value is an outlier?
questions.explanation: The interquartile range is \(\mathrm{IQR}=50-20=30\). The upper fence is \(Q_3+1.5\mathrm{IQR}=50+1.5(30)=50+45=95\). Since \(100>95\), the value \(100\) is an outlier. The value \(90\) is not an outlier because \(90<95\).
questions.hint: Compute the upper fence \(Q_3+1.5\mathrm{IQR}\), then compare each candidate value with that fence.

questions.concept: Missing Quartile from a Box Plot
questions.learningObjective: Determine the upper quartile when the lower quartile and interquartile range are known.
questions.question: A box plot has minimum \(=10\), \(Q_1=14\), median \(=18\), maximum \(=30\), and interquartile range \(12\). Find \(Q_3\).
questions.explanation: The interquartile range satisfies \(\mathrm{IQR}=Q_3-Q_1\). Thus \(12=Q_3-14\), so \(Q_3=14+12=26\).
questions.hint: Use the relationship \(\mathrm{IQR}=Q_3-Q_1\) and solve for the unknown upper quartile.

questions.concept: Effect of Adding a Constant on a Box Plot
questions.learningObjective: Determine how adding a constant to every data value affects the box plot.
questions.question: If every value in a data set is increased by \(5\), which statement about its box plot is true?

options.label: A
options.text: The box shifts right by \(5\), and the interquartile range is unchanged.

options.label: B
options.text: The box shifts right by \(5\), and the interquartile range increases by \(5\).

questions.explanation: Adding the same constant \(5\) to every observation shifts all five-number summary values, including \(Q_1\), the median, and \(Q_3\), to the right by \(5\). Therefore the whole box shifts right by \(5\). The interquartile range is \(Q_3-Q_1\), and both quartiles increase by \(5\), so their difference remains unchanged.
questions.hint: Consider how addition of a constant affects both quartiles in \(Q_3-Q_1\).

questions.concept: Symmetry of the Middle 50 Percent in a Box Plot
questions.learningObjective: Interpret symmetry of the box in a box plot from its quartiles and median.
questions.question: A box plot has \(Q_1=12\), median \(=16\), and \(Q_3=20\). Which statement is correct?

options.label: A
options.text: The median is centered within the box because it is equally distant from \(Q_1\) and \(Q_3\).

options.label: B
options.text: The entire data set must be symmetric about the median.

questions.explanation:
The distances from the median to the two quartiles are
\[
16-12=4
\]
and
\[
20-16=4.
\]
Therefore, the median is centered within the box. Equal distances within the box do not prove that the observations in the middle \(50\%\), the whiskers, or the entire data set are symmetrically distributed.
questions.hint: Compare \(16-12\) with \(20-16\), and interpret only the median's position inside the box.

questions.concept: Outlier Detection from a Five-Number Summary
questions.learningObjective: Apply the \(1.5\times \mathrm{IQR}\) rule to decide whether the maximum value is an outlier.
questions.question: A box plot has five-number summary \(5,10,15,25,60\). Is the maximum value \(60\) an outlier by the \(1.5\times \mathrm{IQR}\) rule?

options.label: A
options.text: Yes, because \(60\) is greater than the upper fence \(47.5\).

options.label: B
options.text: No, because the maximum value is always the endpoint of the upper whisker.

questions.explanation: The interquartile range is \(\mathrm{IQR}=25-10=15\). The upper fence is \(Q_3+1.5\mathrm{IQR}=25+1.5(15)=25+22.5=47.5\). Since \(60>47.5\), the value \(60\) is an outlier by the \(1.5\times \mathrm{IQR}\) rule.
questions.hint: Compute the upper fence using \(Q_3+1.5\mathrm{IQR}\), then compare it with the maximum value.
